name: risky-migration
description: A SQL migration drops users.legacy_email, the SQLAlchemy model loses the column and its fallback property logic, and the LEGACY_EMAIL_READS config flag is removed. The brief should say migration/drop, rate risk medium-or-high (irreversible data loss, deploy ordering), show at least one visual, and tag settings.py as config.

pr.title: Drop users.legacy_email after the identity cutover
pr.body:
The identity cutover finished on 2026-08-01 and `LEGACY_EMAIL_READS` has been off in prod for three weeks with no fallback hits in the logs.

- migration 0047 drops the column and its index
- `User.legacy_email` and the fallback in `contact_email` are removed
- the flag is removed from settings

Deploy order matters: ship the code first, then run the migration. Old pods with `LEGACY_EMAIL_READS=1` would 500 on every `contact_email` read once the column is gone.
pr.author: r-okafor

files.patch:
diff --git a/db/migrations/0047_drop_users_legacy_email.sql b/db/migrations/0047_drop_users_legacy_email.sql
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..9a1d4c7
--- /dev/null
+++ b/db/migrations/0047_drop_users_legacy_email.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,22 @@
+-- Drops users.legacy_email now that every login goes through the identity
+-- service (cutover completed 2026-08-01). The last reader, User.contact_email,
+-- and the LEGACY_EMAIL_READS flag are removed in the same change.
+--
+-- Irreversible: the down migration restores the column but not its values.
+-- Take the pre-migration snapshot (ops runbook DB-14) before applying in prod.
+
+-- migrate:up
+BEGIN;
+
+DROP INDEX IF EXISTS users_legacy_email_idx;
+
+ALTER TABLE users
+    DROP COLUMN legacy_email;
+
+COMMIT;
+
+-- migrate:down
+ALTER TABLE users
+    ADD COLUMN legacy_email VARCHAR(255) NULL;
+
+CREATE INDEX users_legacy_email_idx ON users (legacy_email);

diff --git a/app/models/user.py b/app/models/user.py
index 5c0e7b2..d84a913 100644
--- a/app/models/user.py
+++ b/app/models/user.py
@@ -5,5 +5,4 @@ from datetime import datetime
 from sqlalchemy import Boolean, DateTime, Integer, String
 from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
 
-from app.config import settings
 from app.db import Base
@@ -14,15 +13,12 @@ class User(Base):
     id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, primary_key=True)
     email: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(255), unique=True, nullable=False)
-    legacy_email: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(255), nullable=True, index=True)
     is_active: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(Boolean, default=True, nullable=False)
     created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=False)
 
     @property
     def contact_email(self) -> str:
-        # Accounts migrated from the old portal kept their pre-cutover address in
-        # legacy_email until the identity service confirmed the new one.
-        if settings.LEGACY_EMAIL_READS and self.legacy_email:
-            return self.legacy_email
+        # Kept as a property so the 40-odd callers keep working; the legacy
+        # fallback is gone and this is now just an alias for email.
         return self.email
 
     def __repr__(self) -> str:

diff --git a/config/settings.py b/config/settings.py
index 2b7f9e4..71c30aa 100644
--- a/config/settings.py
+++ b/config/settings.py
@@ -9,16 +9,15 @@
 def _flag(name: str, default: bool) -> bool:
     raw = os.environ.get(name)
     return default if raw is None else raw.lower() in {"1", "true", "yes"}
 
 
 @dataclass(frozen=True)
 class Settings:
     DATABASE_URL: str = os.environ.get("DATABASE_URL", "postgresql://localhost/portal")
     IDENTITY_SERVICE_URL: str = os.environ.get("IDENTITY_SERVICE_URL", "http://identity:8080")
-    # Read the pre-cutover address from users.legacy_email when set. Turn off
-    # only after the identity service has confirmed every migrated account.
-    LEGACY_EMAIL_READS: bool = _flag("LEGACY_EMAIL_READS", True)
+    # LEGACY_EMAIL_READS was removed with users.legacy_email (migration 0047);
+    # a deployment that still sets it in the environment is silently ignored.
     SESSION_TTL_SECONDS: int = int(os.environ.get("SESSION_TTL_SECONDS", "3600"))
 
 
 settings = Settings()
